gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.

gaps.sentence: The new bridge ___ (open) by the mayor next month.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + opened, with the agent in a by-phrase.

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: The road ___ at the moment — use the bypass.
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' — present continuous passive: is being repaired.

gaps.sentence: These wetlands ___ (threaten) by pollution every single year.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive with the agent introduced by 'by': are threatened by.

gaps.sentence: Her memoir ___ (translate) into fourteen languages so far.
gaps.explanation: 'So far' requires present perfect passive: has been + translated (singular 'memoir').

gaps.sentence: A final decision ___ (MAKE) once the consultation ends.
gaps.explanation: The decision does not make itself: future passive will be made.

gaps.sentence: By the time the reporters arrived, the evidence ___ (destroy).
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle for the action completed before the arrival.
